title: Latent friction deck + customer lab journal
content:
Purpose: quick, workshop-friendly synthesis of recent customer interviews, prioritized micro-probes (safe experiments), and a compact deck outline we can use with Eng/Product to scope low-effort fixes. Not a final roadmap — this is a lab journal of friction we can poke over 1–3 sprints.

Background / why this exists:
- Last 6 weeks: 12 enterprise interviews (~30–45m each) + incoming CS tickets flagged as "platform friction". Pattern: teams are blocked by opaque cost signals, surprising latency at scale, and brittle routing behavior when traffic spikes.
- Interviews included customers on Hosted API (6), Dedicated (3), Private (3). Mix of AI-native startups and mid-market product teams.

Field vignettes (raw, lightly edited):
1) "We hit an unexpected 3x cost spike when we moved from dev to prod — the real culprit was unexpected prompt prefix duplication across calls; hard to debug" — mid-market search product.
2) "Can we pin a model that is smaller but deterministic when latency budget tightens? Our rollout reverted to a bigger variant and user flows spiked" — fintech start-up on Dedicated.
3) "KV cache feels like magic — would love to see what is cached, hit rate, and eviction events so we can tune prompts" — healthcare product on Private.

Latent friction themes (synthesis):
- Observability blindspots: token-level cost attribution, prefix duplication detection, KV-cache telemetry.
- Routing surprises: automatic fallbacks to higher-cost regions/variants without clear audit trail.
- Developer ergonomics: tuning batch size/latency SLO is opaque; safe defaults helpful but not adjustable per-route.
- Ops safety: rollback stories are brittle when model variants diverge in output quality.

Top micro-probes (prioritized by expected impact / implementation effort):
A) Probe: "Token-heat snapshot" (low effort) — add a lightweight export that shows token spend per route for last 24h, bucketed by prompt size and model variant.
   Hypothesis: immediate reduction in debugging time; customers will spot prefix duplication.
   Success metric: median debug time down 30% on pilot customers.

B) Probe: "KV cache inspector" (med effort) — expose per-customer cache hit/miss rate and a sample of cached prefixes (scrubbed) + eviction events.
   Hypothesis: teams will tune prompt prefixing and see cost reductions.
   Risk: PII; needs sanitizer + opt-in.

C) Probe: "Fallback audit trail" (low-med) — when smart routing switches variant/region, record a structured event with reason, cost delta, and link to matching request traces.
   Hypothesis: reduces surprises and helps SREs avoid noisy escalations.

D) Probe: "Per-route batching knob" (med effort) — simple per-route override for max batch latency vs throughput with a UI toggle and API flag.
   Hypothesis: high-impact for teams with mixed latency/throughput flows.

E) Probe: "Canary pin + deterministic fallback" (higher effort) — allow pinning a stable, smaller model variant for stated percentage of traffic; automatic deterministic fallback policy for quality regressions.
   Hypothesis: reduces accidental rollouts to costlier variants.

Patch sketches / minimal UX flows (to take to Eng):
- Token-heat snapshot: route -> date-range selector -> small chart + downloadable CSV. Quick endpoint: GET /routes/{id}/token-heat?days=1
- KV inspector: opt-in flag per-org; sanitized sample rows + hit/miss counters; integrate into Console > Routes > Cache tab.
- Fallback audit trail: append structured events to request trace entries with links in Console trace viewer.

Privacy & security notes:
- Any sample-based probes (KV inspector) must run through existing DLP sanitizers and default to opt-out. Legal flagged P0 if we export cached plaintext prompts by default.

Potential quick wins (<=2 wk effort):
- Token-heat snapshot (A) + small Console panel.
- Fallback audit trail (C) as extra fields in existing traces.

Medium-term (2–8 wk):
- KV cache inspector with opt-in and sanitizer pipeline.
- Per-route batching knob with safe default and SDK flag.

Longer-term (quarter+):
- Canary pin/fallback policy automation and rollout UI.

Open questions / unknowns to validate with Eng/Product in the workshop:
- Storage cost / retention policy for token-heat and fallback events.
- Sanitization rules / who owns DLP gating for cache inspection.
- Backwards compatibility with Dedicated customers who manage their own infra.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Workshop with Product + Observability (90m) — present this doc + 2 customer vignettes. Attendees: Product-hosted-api, eng-observability, CS AE owners.
2) Quick spike ticket for Token-heat: ETA 7 days; small UX wire + data-export.
3) Draft privacy brief and run by Legal for KV inspector opt-in language.

Meeting artifacts to bring: 2 anonymized interview transcripts (attached in linked artifacts), current Route tracing sample, cost-analytics schema.

Decision log (for the journal):
- 2026-05-01: choose token-heat as the first probe (low-effort, high-visibility).
- 2026-05-03: schedule Product workshop; need SRE presence.

Notes to self / rough phrases for slides: 
- "Make cost legible — not just visible."
- "Cache is a resource; give teams a window into it."
- "Small audit trails prevent big surprises."

Appendix: Suggested slides for 6–8 min sync (slide titles / bullets):
1) One-slide problem statement + 3 vignettes.
2) Latent friction themes (observability / routing / ergonomics).
3) Top 5 probes (A–E) with expected effort and impact.
4) Quick wins and privacy guardrails.
5) Ask from Eng/Product: allocation for spike + review cadence.

End of lab journal entry.

(Feel free to edit the vignettes to anonymize further before sharing externally.)
